solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's a very odd location to store your clothes

indicators.note: odd suggests something peculiar or out of the ordinary, so these letters are set out strangely

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a wardrobe has been put in a very strange spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' reads as a comment on the location, but it signals that the letters of IT'S A VERY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestiary is a robing room or cloakroom, a place where garments are kept.

clue.text: Huge salaries ultimately swallowed up by tax

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed inside the tax, placed within it

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of salaries is used

explanation.surface: Big pay packets end up being eaten away by taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, value added tax, is a sales tax charged in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast and huge are synonyms, both meaning immensely large.

clue.text: Quashes issue from a previous relationship?

definitions.meaning: to quash something is to step on it, stamp it out
issue means offspring; a partner's son from an earlier relationship

explanation.surface: Someone suppresses a problem left over from a past affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem but means children. Split the answer as STEPS ON for the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a spouse's son from a prior marriage or partnership, so offspring of that relationship.

clue.text: Pose as one individual in couple

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to couple animals is to mate them
an individual is a person

explanation.surface: A single person pretends to be part of a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To impersonate someone is to pretend to be them, passing yourself off as them.

clue.text: Extremely reclusive mammal is close again

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last of reclusive

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal

explanation.surface: A very shy animal hides away once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reseal a container is to shut it up once more after opening.

clue.text: Group boycotted on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a boycotted product or person is banned

explanation.surface: A pop group finds its songs refused airplay by radio stations.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians, or any group of people acting together.

clue.text: A cereal and fruit

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A bowl of breakfast cereal served with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak tree, botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Not looking forward to days studying

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day or days
reading a subject means studying it, especially at a British university

explanation.surface: A student is fearful of the long days of revision ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading something means anticipating it with fear, the opposite of eager anticipation.

clue.text: Demanding part of process consumes energy

indicators.note: the stage swallows the energy, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a step is one stage of a process
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: One stage of a procedure is especially tiring because it uses up a lot of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep price or task is excessive, making heavy demands.

clue.text: In the end, directors snub Italian females

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, taken here from directors

parts.note: to snub someone is to ignore them

explanation.surface: A board of directors finally decides to cold-shoulder some Italian women.
explanation.definitionFit: Signore is the plural of signora, the Italian title or word for a married woman or lady.

clue.text: Go and settle around California

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to move and make a home somewhere in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a location word but tells you to rearrange GO AND SETTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden State is the official nickname of California, from its gold rush.

clue.text: Smooth emerald isn't warped

indicators.note: something warped is bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A jeweller notes that a polished emerald has no distortion.
explanation.definitionFit: Streamlined shapes are sleek, with flowing contours that offer little resistance.

clue.text: Current politician played a role and had influence

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
an MP is a Member of Parliament
an actor who played a role acted

explanation.surface: A sitting member of parliament once went on stage and made a difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Impacted, used as a verb, means affected something, made an impression upon it.

clue.text: One advising me to start to relax around noon

indicators.note: the other pieces go round the abbreviation, so it sits inside them
the start of a word is its opening letter, taken here from relax

explanation.surface: Someone advises the speaker to take a break around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals insertion: the abbreviation for noon goes inside the run of other pieces rather than round them, landing between the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is an experienced counsellor who guides and advises a less experienced person.

clue.text: Rucksack carried by climber, generally

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the letters of these words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A mountaineer usually has a backpack along on the climb.
explanation.walkthrough: A bergen is a large rucksack, a name associated especially with the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergen is a name for a large backpack, especially military issue, from a Norwegian maker.

clue.text: Attraction leads to great, long-lasting romance

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters, taken from great and long-lasting

parts.note: an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: Allure results in a wonderful, enduring love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring charm or appeal, a kind of attractiveness.

clue.text: Rickety train touring a European city

indicators.note: the jumbled letters travel round the single letter, enclosing it
something rickety is shaky and likely to fall apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shaky old train carries tourists round a city in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' turns TRAIN into TIRNA, and 'touring' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania, in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Ace air cadets, possibly circling island and body of water

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation, enclosing it
possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Excellent air cadets fly round an island over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AIR CADETS to DRIATCSEA, and 'circling' puts I inside it to give DRIATICSEA, after A for Ace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic Sea is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans.

clue.text: Cold space, we're told

indicators.note: being told something is hearing it, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: We hear it is a chilly area.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is watery discharge from the nose or eyes, as with a common cold.

clue.text: Papers maybe left alongside entrance to executive lounge

parts.note: identity papers are ID

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter, from executive

explanation.surface: Documents are left beside the doorway into a business-class lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room, the executive lounge, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to laze around, to be idle.

clue.text: Tears flowing about man and woman

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the pronoun, enclosing it
flowing suggests fluid movement, so these letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Tears stream down over a man and a woman, a scene of emotional parting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' makes TRESA, and 'about' wraps those letters round the pronoun; 'man and woman' tempts you to look for two definitions, but only 'woman' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Get out of the way of a vacuum

definitions.text: Get out of the way of

parts.note: a vacuum is an empty space, a void

explanation.surface: Someone steps aside to dodge a vacuum cleaner being pushed along.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep clear of it or steer away from it.

clue.text: March taking place in Pride month

indicators.note: the answer occurs within these words, sitting in their letters

explanation.surface: A parade is held during the month of Pride celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like a month, fitting the surface, but it is the protest sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a demonstration, a protest walk through the streets.

clue.text: Happy nurse, say, almost off duty

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a nurse is one example of a carer
someone off duty is free

explanation.surface: A nurse is cheerful at the end of a shift, nearly finished work.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree describes someone untroubled and light-hearted, without worries.
